key_insight: CatDiT is a unified diffusion-transformer framework that generates novel catalyst structures while simultaneously controlling adsorbate type, binding energy, and catalyst class.
engineering_relevance: It enables faster, property-directed inverse design of heterogeneous catalysts across broad chemical spaces, helping prioritize candidates for targeted reactions like nitrogen reduction.
method: Learns compressed latent representations for efficient training and fast sampling.
Uses a diffusion transformer to generate valid catalyst structures from intermetallic alloys to oxide surfaces.
Supports multi-conditional generation with both discrete-property control and directional continuous-property control.
evidence_signal: For NRR, multi-conditional generation produced 28 DFT-relaxed alloy candidates meeting the target activity window and above the pure-metal *N-*H scaling line, giving about a 1.5× enrichment over the source distribution.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated in a specific NRR screening setting, so transferability to other reactions and chemically more complex catalyst families may require additional validation.
paper_title: Catalyst Diffusion Transformer: Generative Inverse Design of Heterogeneous Catalysts
